text: Abdul Hamid Hamidi (7 January 1927 – 11 July 2019) was a field hockey player from Pakistan, born in Bannu. He scored 48 international goals in 55 appearances for the Pakistan national team. He won a silver medal at the 1956 Summer Olympics and served as captain of the gold medal-winning team at the 1960 Summer Olympics. After retiring from professional play, he managed the national team during the 1966 and 1970 Asian Games and held the position of secretary general of the Pakistan Hockey Federation. As of 2017, he resided in Islamabad. He passed away on 11 July 2019 at the Combined Military Hospital in Rawalpindi at the age of 92. This article about a Pakistani Olympic medalist is a stub.
